subclassFeature.name: School of Hard Knocks
entries: Wizardry requires years of training and careful study to cultivate. Even then, most wizards only truly master a single discipline of magic. However, away from the universities and textbooks, there exist other, less refined ways to develop a connection with the arcane. Through diligent observation of the other more fortunate students, and the magic of the everyday world, self-taught Wizards have been known to emerge. These selfstarters are referred to scathingly by some and proudly by others as Wizards of the School of Hard Knocks.

subclassFeature.name: Observational Savant
entries: Starting at level 2, you have developed an incredible awareness and connection to magic after years of observation and personal study. Whenever you see a spell cast by another spellcaster, you may roll an arcana check (DC = 10+ that spell's level). On a success, if that spell is a Wizard spell, you may copy it into your spellbook within the next 48 hours, after which time you forget the details of the spell if it goes uncopied. The time and gold you spend to copy a spell in this manner is halved.

subclassFeature.name: Running on Empty
entries: Starting at 2nd level, when you cast a spell using your final spell slot, or cast a cantrip while you have no remaining spell slots, you can instantly recover any number of spell slots that have a combined level equal to or less than half your wizard level, rounded up.
Regaining spells in this way is extremely taxing. When you do so, you gain one point of {@condition exhaustion} and cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Hard Knock Life
entries: Beginning at 6th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning damage, your current hit point maximum increases by 6, and whenever you gain a wizard level, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 1 point.

subclassFeature.name: Streetwise
entries: Beginning at 10th level, you may add your intelligence modifier to wisdom checks and wisdom saving throws. In addition, when you take the help action, the creature you are helping may add your intelligence modifier to their check.

subclassFeature.name: Self-Made Mage
entries: Starting at 14th level, as an action, you can draw on your vast, worldly experience to produce a single, empowering burst of magic. Chose one of the following effects:

items: You gain immunity to a damage type of your choice for one minute.
You gain a flying speed, swimming speed, and burrow speed equal to your walking speed for 10 minutes.
You have advantage on all saving throws for one minute.
You have advantage on all ranged attack rolls for one minute.
When you next cast a spell that requires a creature to make a saving throw, treat that creature's result on the die as a 1.

entries: One you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Bloodline
entries: The innate magic that flows through your veins is Demonic in origin, a dark power that burns with a desire to be wielded in battle. Often, Sorcerers with this origin can trace their powers back to a dark bargain or blood pact made by an ancestor with a powerful Demon, or even claim a parent as one possessed by a Demon. Sometimes, these powers manifest in individuals seemingly at random, perhaps as a result of the unknowable machinations of a powerful Demon Lord in another realm of existence, or as an unpredictable, chaotic burst of Demonic energy latching onto a host.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Demonic Spellcasting table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be a {@filter conjuration or necromancy spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list|spells|class=sorcerer;warlock;wizard|school=C;N|level=1;2;3;4;5;6;7;8;9}.

entries.caption: Demonic Spellcasting
rows: 1st
{@spell Thaumaturgy}, {@spell Bane}, {@spell Inflict Wounds}
3rd
{@spell Darkness}, {@spell Levitate}
5th
{@spell Animate Dead}, {@spell Fear}
7th
{@spell Phantasmal Killer}, {@spell Banishment}
9th
{@spell Contact Other Plane}, {@spell Planar Binding}

subclassFeature.name: Dark Wanderer
entries: Starting at 1st level, you have {@sense Darkvision} at a range of 60ft, and you can read and write Abyssal or one other language of your choice. In addition, whenever you cast a spell that would create magical darkness, you and a number of creatures you designate equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) can treat that magical darkness as though it were non-magical darkness (allowing for creatures with {@sense Darkvision} to see in it, for example).
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Sorcerous Frenzy
entries: Starting at 6th level, whenever you kill a hostile enemy humanoid, celestial or fiend you regain 2 sorcery points.
Additionally, you can use your sorcery points to enhance yourself. As a bonus action, you can spend any number of sorcery points to grant yourself 5x that many temporary hit points.
Once you use this feature to gain temporary hit points, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Transformation
entries: Starting at 14th level, as a bonus action, you can unleash the chaotic, demonic energy within you, enhancing your abilities for the next 10 minutes. Roll twice on the table below to randomly determine the benefits you recieve, rerolling any duplicates.

items: You grow skeletal wings, have a fly speed of 40 ft, can hover, and your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

Your hands become long, sharp talons. Your reach increases by 5ft, and you can use your action to make two unarmed strikes, dealing {@damage 1d12} magical slashing damage on each hit. You can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity modifier, for the attack and damage rolls.
You turn {@condition invisible} and can communicate telepathically with any creature that speaks at least one language within 120ft of you.
You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spells you cast cannot be counterspelled or dispelled, except by an {@spell antimagic field}.
Even if you cast a spell with a casting time of a bonus action, you can still cast a levelled spell as your action, as long as that spell has a casting time of one action.
Whenever you cast a spell, you may treat that spell as though it were cast at one level higher than you cast it.
You have resistance to all non-magical damage, and have advantage on all saving throws to maintain concentration on a spell.

entries: Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 6 sorcery points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Familiar
entries: Starting at 18th level, once per long rest, as an action, you can call forth a demon to aid you in battle. A {@creature Hezrou} appears at a point you choose within 60ft of you. You can command it as a free action, and it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your commands and is hostile to everyone except you and your allies. It lasts for 59 minutes, or until its hit points reach 0, at which point it vanishes.
In addition, the {@creature Hezrou} gains the following benefits:

items.entry: If the {@creature Hezrou} forces an enemy to make a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.
When summoned, the {@creature Hezrou} gains temporary hit points equal to your Sorcerer level + your charisma modifier.

You gain the damage immunities and resistances of the {@creature Hezrou}, and it gains any damage resistances and immunities you have, for as long as you are within 60ft of each other and neither of you are {@condition incapacitated}.

subclassFeature.name: The Deep Consciousness
entries: Your Patron is The Deep Consciousness, an enigmatic and mysterious presence, unknowable and unyielding, existing without form. It is a void, empty of both light and darkness. A vast, incredible, ancient mind untethered to flesh or machine, holding unfathomable knowledge and understanding beyond the limits of mortal comprehension.
The Deep Consciousness grants power to Warlocks, steadily spreading its influence across all planes of existence in the aim of furthering some unknowable agenda.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Deep Consciousness lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a Warlock Spell. The following spells are added to the Warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Expanded Spell List
rows: 1st
{@spell Disguise Self}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter||Hideous Laughter}
2nd
{@spell Blindness/Deafness}, {@spell Silence}
3rd
{@spell Sending}, {@spell Slow}
4th
{@spell Compulsion}, {@spell Confusion}
5th
{@spell Modify Memory}, {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond||Telepathic Bond}
9th
{@spell Weird}

subclassFeature.name: Iron Mind
entries: The power of The Deep Consciousness has strengthened your mind. At 1st level, you gain resistance to psychic damage, and you can add your charisma modifier to your intelligence saving throws.

In addition, if you would drop concentration on a spell cast using your pact magic, you can choose to maintain concentration instead. You can use this ability an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Invasion
entries: Beginning at 6th level you can use a bonus action to strike at the mind of a target you can see within 60ft of you that has an intelligence score of 3 or higher. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock Spell Save DC. On a failed save it suffers one negative effect of your choice from the following list:

items: It is {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn
It is {@condition deafened} until the end of your next turn
Its base movement speed is reduced by 30ft until the end of your next turn
It falls {@condition prone}
It drops concentration on any spell it is concentrating on
The first time it takes damage each turn, it takes an additional {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. This effect ends at the end of your next turn.

entries: Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Fortress
entries: When you reach 10th level, your mental fortifications grow even more powerful. You are immune to the {@condition charmed} and {@condition frightened} conditions. In addition, whenever you cast a spell that would charm or frighten an enemy, or use your 6th level Mental Invasion ability, you may expend an additional Pact Magic spell slot to have the target make its saving throw to resist the effect with disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Mind Crush
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can expend your energies to open a doorway in a target's mind to allow a small vestige of your Patron's power to invade.

As an action, choose a creature you can see within 60ft of you. Both you and it are {@condition incapacitated} and your base movement speeds become 0 for the next minute, or until you chose to end the effect. At the end of each of its turns, or whenever it takes damage from another source, it takes {@damage 2d10} psychic damage and makes a wisdom saving throw, freeing itself from your control on a successful save. Creatures immune to psychic damage treat damage from this effect as though they were resistant to it, not immune.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Demon Fist
entries: Monks of the Way of the Demon Fist train ferociously in the art of martial combat. They learn ruthless techniques to grievously wound, {@condition incapacitated|incapacitate}, or kill their enemies with blinding speed, harnessing their ki as a deadly weapon to bolster their power or devastate their foe.

subclassFeature.name: The Hidden Demon Technique
entries: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate the flow of your ki to duplicate the effects of certain spells, cursing an enemy or empowering yourself.
As an action, you can spend 2 ki points to cast {@spell Hold Person}, {@spell Blur}, {@spell Alter Self}, or {@spell Blindness/Deafness} at their lowest level without providing material components.
Additionally, you gain the {@spell Thaumaturgy} cantrip if you don't already have it.

subclassFeature.name: Ferocious Strike
entries: At 6th level, your strikes become brutal, targeting pressure points, aiming to grievously wound or kill. You score a critical hit on a 19 or a 20, and any creature you strike with a melee attack can't regain hit points until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Fighting Spirit
entries: By 11th level, your fighting spirit has become so intense that pain only fuels your frenzy. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to instantly make two unarmed strikes against any creature within 5ft of you.

subclassFeature.name: Fury of the Demon
entries: At 17th level, you gain the ability to devastate a foe by swiftly striking at multiple pressure points. If you hit the same creature with four or more melee attacks in one turn, at the end of that turn, that creature takes an additional {@damage 8d10} force damage and falls {@condition prone}.

subclassFeature.name: Kingpin
entries: In a world of monsters and magic, there are many ways to get rich. Some rogues steal. It could be a coin purse here, or a gold necklace there, but you have your eyes set on a grander, less tangible goal. Organised crime is big business, and any business needs good management to enjoy the lion's share. You have the skills to protect yourself, but what is a leader without disposable goons to aid them in the dirty work? As you increase in power and notoriety, so too will your influence through the underbelly of society grow. Many Kingpins operate outside the law, but some are known to conduct operations on behalf of the state, in businesses such as bodyguarding, monster hunting, and debt collection.

subclassFeature.name: Unarmed and Dangerous
entries: You have trained in a manner that allows you to maintain an outward appearance of respectability and dignity. Openly carrying a weapon is uncouth and bound to attract the wrong type of attention. Fortunately, you are just as deadly without one.
Starting at 3rd level, you gain the following benefits.

items: You gain proficiency with improvised weapons, and you may apply your sneak attack bonus to your unarmed strikes and attacks with improvised weapons.
You may use your dexterity modifier instead of strength when calculating attack and damage rolls using unarmed strikes and improvised weapon attacks.
Your unarmed strikes use a d4 for damage. This increases to a d6 at level 11.

subclassFeature.name: Tough Guy
entries: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in {@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion} (your choice) and your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your rogue level + your charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Thug Dealer
entries: Starting at 9th level, your influence has grown to the extent that you can conscript a Thug to accompany you in your daily dealings. They are friendly to you and your companions, and obey your commands. Your Thug's loyalty is absolute, however they may disobey blatantly suicidal orders at your DM's discretion.
Find your Thug's game statistics in the {@creature Thug|DMSecretWeapon} stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.

In combat, the Thug shares your initiative count, but they take their turn immediately after yours. They can move and use their reaction on their own, but the only actions they can take on their turn are the help action or the dodge action, unless you use a bonus action on your turn to command them to take another action.
That action can be one in their stat block or some other action. If you are {@condition incapacitated}, the Thug can take any action their choice.

If your Thug dies, you must return their equipment and body to their loved ones (if possible) and also give the family 500 gold pieces as a mark of respect. If you do not, your reputation sours and you cannot conscript a replacement Thug.

subclassFeature.name: I'll Do It Myself
entries: Starting at 13th level, you can use a bonus action to crack your knuckles, menacingly. Add your charisma modifier to your next attack attack roll and your next damage roll this turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your charisma modifier per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Goon Platoon
entries: When you reach 17th level, you can now conscript up to two thugs with your Thug Dealer trait, and any Thugs under your command gain temporary hit points equal to your charisma modifier any time you roll for initiative.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Totem Avatar
entries: The Circle of the Totem Avatar is an ancient order of Druids that harness the spiritual energies of the earth and manifest them in the form of powerful, totem armor. They cloak themselves in a spiritual avatar, amplifying their size and power. The form a druid's Totem Avatar takes often reflects an aspect of their personality or beliefs. An aggressive, hard headed druid may form themselves a Beast Totem Avatar in the form of a mighty bull, whereas a contemplative and subtle druid's Beast Totem Avatar may take the shape of an owl.

subclassFeature.name: Totemic Transformation
entries: Starting at 2nd level, as a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape to conjure spectral Totem Armor around your body, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain temporary hit points equal to your Druid level x3 for as long as your Totem Armor remains.
Your size becomes large, if there is room to do so.
Your reach increases by 5ft.

entries: In addition, choose one of the following forms: Beast, Tree, or Golem. The form you choose confers additional benefits.

entries.name: Beast Form
entries: You can use your Wisdom modifier when calculating attack and damage rolls for your unarmed strikes.
When you take the attack action on your turn, you can make a number of totemic unarmed strikes equal to half your Wisdom Modifier (rounded down).
Your totemic unarmed strikes deal {@damage 1d6} force damage.

entries.name: Tree Form
entries: Whenever you cast a leveled spell, you can bless one creature within 30ft of you with temporary hit points equal to that spell's level + your wisdom modifier.
You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
You are immune to the {@condition Stunned}, {@condition Paralyzed} and {@condition Prone} conditions.

entries.name: Golem Form
entries: You resist Bludgeoning, Slashing and Piercing damage from weapon attacks.
You have advantage on Strength and Constitution Saving Throws.
Your Totem Armor lasts for 1 minute, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}, Wild Shape, or use your Totemic Activation feature again to shift forms.

subclassFeature.name: Guardian Soul
entries: From 6th level, your Totem Armor offers you a measure of protection against lethal damage. Whenever you would fall to 0 hit points or die while in your Totemic Transformation, you instead fall to 1 hit point and your Totemic Transformation ends.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Totemic Transformation
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can enhance your totem forms with a greater level of power. Your Totem transformations gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Beast
entries: Your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistances and immunities, and if you take the attack action on your turn, you can make a single totemic unarmed strike as a bonus action.

entries.name: Tree
entries: You have 30ft of Tremorsense, and you can cast spells with a range of touch targeting a creature up to 30 ft away from you, as long as both you and that target are touching the ground.

entries.name: Golem
entries: You are resistant to fire, cold and poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: Totem Unification
entries: By expending two uses of your Wild Shape, you can activate all forms of your Totem Armor simultaneously, gaining the benefits of all of the totem forms at once.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Calamity
entries: Calamity Barbarians draw upon the raw, primal energies of the material plane. They embrace the reality that the forces of nature rule above all. Earthquakes topple the mightiest of kingdoms; tidal waves decimate the greatest fleets.
Contrary to what the cruellest tyrants and noblest kings may wish to believe, there are no heights mortals can reach that cannot be torn asunder by natural disaster.

Embracing this chaotic power, a Calamity Barbarian's greataxe may be struck by lightning as it falls in a blast of power, or a javelin may ignite in flame as it soars through the air. When angered, they are a walking natural disaster, channelling the immeasurable wrath of a calamity.

subclassFeature.name: Imbued Calamity
entries: When you take this path at 3rd level, choose one calamity through which you channel your power. Each calamity has an associated damage type, which empowers some of your other abilities, and confers a special benefit to you.

subclassFeature.name: Earthquake
entries: Bludgeoning Damage - Your base your walking speed increases by 5ft.

subclassFeature.name: Volcano
entries: Fire Damage - You gain a resistance to fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Hurricane
entries: Lightning Damage - You gain a resistance to lightning damage.

subclassFeature.name: Tsunami
entries: Cold Damage - You gain a resistance to cold damage.

subclassFeature.name: Disaster Strike
entries: Also at level 3, while you are raging, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can channel a calamitous strike, dealing {@damage 4d4} additional damage of your associated calamity type.
You can only use this feature once per long rest, unless you expend one use of your rage to do it again.
The damage of your Disaster Strike increases to {@damage 4d6} at level 6, {@damage 4d8} at level 10, and {@damage 4d10} at level 14.

subclassFeature.name: Oncoming Calamity
entries: Beginning at 6th level, your calamitous power grows. You gain an additional power related to your associated calamity type.

entries.name: Earthquake
entries: You gain the ability to sense the vibrations and tremors in the earth around you. You have Tremorsense in a 10ft range.

entries.name: Volcano
entries: You glow red hot while raging. Any creature grappling or grappled by you takes fire damage at the start of each of its turns equal to twice your proficiency bonus. You have resistance to cold damage.

entries.name: Tsunami
entries: You are a devastating threat in water. You gain a swim speed equal to twice your walking speed, and can hold your breath for up to an hour below water. You have resistance to fire damage.

entries.name: Hurricane
entries: You are empowered by the force of winds. While raging, you can choose to hover 5ft above the ground. In addition, as a bonus action while raging, you can leap through the air supported by a conjured gale. You can leap a number of feet equal to 3x your proficiency bonus in this way. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Invoke Calamity
entries: Starting at 10th level, your connection with the forces of elemental chaos allows you to force calamities on others.

When a creature within 15ft of you makes an attack roll against a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that attack (before the roll). If that attack misses, the attacking creature takes magical damage of your associated calamity damage type equal to half your barbarian level.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Calamity Incarnate
entries: At 14th level, while raging, once per long rest, you use a bonus action to expend an additional use of your rage and transcend into a maelstrom of living elemental power; a natural disaster incarnate.
This transformation lasts for as long as you are raging. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you invoke this transformation, creatures of your choice within 10ft of you take {@damage 2d6} magical damage of your calamity damage type.
Your movement speed increases by 10ft.
The area in a 15ft radius of you becomes difficult terrain for any creature other than yourself.
Your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d6} magical damage of your calamity damage type.
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack, that creature must make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + Strength Modifier + Proficiency Bonus) or fall {@condition prone}.

subclassFeature.name: Sky Domain
entries: Sky Domain Clerics are devoted to the open heavens and believe in the ideals of freedom, trust, individualism and tranquility. Deities such as the Greek Titan Uranus, Goddess Hera, Roman God Jupiter, or Egyptian God Horus are example patrons of Sky Clerics. Gods of the sky can also embody the sun, air, righteous combat, personal potential, weather and freedom.

{@spell Feather Fall}, {@spell Thunderwave}
3rd
{@spell Gust of Wind}, {@spell Levitate}
5th
{@spell Call Lightning}, {@spell Sleet Storm}

9th

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with {@filter Martial Weapons|items|type=martial weapon;!treasure (gemstone);!treasure (art object);!futuristic;!renaissance;!treasure (coinage);!modern} and {@item Navigator's Tools|PHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Sky Scout
entries: Also at first level, you learn the {@spell Find Familiar} spell and can cast it as a ritual, except no matter the form your familiar takes, it has a 30ft fly speed, can hover and gains appropriate anatomy to support flight. For example, a Weasel familiar might be granted a pair of spectral wings.

As a bonus action, you can grant your familiar immunity to all damage for the next minute, or until it deals damage to another creature. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Skystrider
entries: At 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to grant the power of flight to those around you.

As an action, you present your holy symbol, and a gentle beam of sunlight shines forth onto a creature within 5ft. They gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Cleric level, a flying speed equal to their walking speed and can hover. These abilities last until they finish a long rest, or you use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Sunlight Empowerment
entries: Starting at 6th level, while in sunlight, you have advantage on attack rolls and {@skill perception} checks that rely on sight.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to imbue your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon Attack, you can cause the Attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Breath of the Heavens
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you use your Skystrider Channel Divinity, you can impart the benefits to a number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus. In addition, allied creatures within 60ft of you with a fly speed can dash as a bonus action, and their movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Tomb Raider
entries: Tomb Raiders are explorers. They are hunters of fantastical treasures and guardians of ancient relics. They seek to plum the depths of history by hand, protecting the historic artefacts of immemorial cultures. They strive to educate, discover and preserve; a tomb raider is far from a common thief.

Exploring long forgotten dungeons and deep burial sites is risky business. Foolish Tomb Raiders don't live long. Adventuring parties and expeditions will often seek the aid of a Tomb Raider to guide them through dangerous dungeons, disarming traps and removing curses. A combination of warrior, locksmith, cursebreaker and artist; a wise Tomb Raider is the difference between a party finding untold magical secrets and items, or finding certain death in the forgotten, dark tombs of the old world.

subclassFeature.name: Favoured Weapon
entries: At third level, choose a Favoured Weapon from the following list. You gain additional benefits while wielding your Favoured Weapon. You can swap a Favoured Weapon choice to another option any time you gain a Ranger Level:

items.name: Whip
entries: Your attacks with a whip deal {@damage 2d4} slashing damage. In addition, when you hit a creature with an attack using a whip, if they are large or smaller, you can use your bonus action to attempt to pull them off their balance. They make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your Dex or Strength modifier+ Proficiency Bonus) or fall {@condition prone}.

items.name: Blowgun
entries: You ignore the loading property of the blowgun, and attacks at long range don't impose disadvantage.

In addition, as a bonus action, you can coat the tip of a number of blowgun darts equal to your proficiency bonus in a simple poison. You have the knowledge on how to harvest this poison from natural resources found in your favoured terrain. Poisoned darts remain venomous for one minute or until they strike a creature. On a hit, the target takes one point of piercing damage and makes a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus), taking an additional {@damage 2d6} poison damage on a failed save.

items.name: Net
entries: You ignore the restriction on nets preventing you from making multiple attacks in a turn. In addition, making an attack roll with a net while standing within 5ft of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your roll, and attacks at long range also don't impose disadvantage.

Finally, your skill with net craftsmanship allows you to create more sturdy and powerful nets. You can craft a sturdy net in one hour of work at the cost of 10 gold pieces. It has an AC of 15, requires 15 slashing damage to break, and requires a strength check ({@dc 15}) to escape from.

subclassFeature.name: Lost Knowledge
entries: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in either history, investigation, or thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make which uses that proficiency.

subclassFeature.name: Raider's Fortune
entries: From 6th level, you have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition poisoned} condition, and advantage on saving throws to avoid or resist the effects of curses and cursed magical items.

In addition, you can cast the spells {@spell Detect Magic}, {@spell Remove Curse} and {@spell Identify} once each per long rest without expending a spell slot. You can also cast these spells with any available spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

subclassFeature.name: Raider's Instinct
entries: Starting at 11th level, you can add your wisdom modifier to any {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Stealth}, or {@skill Investigation} check.
In addition, you may choose an additional weapon from the Favoured Weapon list to act as a second Favoured Weapon, and you gain a +1 to attack rolls with your Favoured Weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Unorthodox Weapon Master
entries: Starting at 15th level, the maximum number of magical items you can attune to increases by one. In addition, when you use the attack action to attack with a Favoured Weapon, you can use your bonus action to make a single attack with a Favoured Weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Spectre Knight
entries: Many warriors kill, but none harness the dread powers of death itself like the Spectre Knight. Forever walking the twilight expanse that stretches between the living and the dead, Spectre Knights are imbued with supernatural, unknowable forces from beyond the realms of natural magic.
Not all Spectre Knight's are agents of chaos and evil, but the inky blackness of death that haunts their journey can push even the most noble warriors down a cruel, dark path.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Magic
entries: At 3rd level, you learn to manifest the power of the dead within yourself. This power is represented in your Spectral Energy dice, which are a {@dice d6}. You have a number of these dice equal to 1 + your proficiency bonus, and they fuel the powers you have, which are detailed below.

Some of your powers expend the Spectral Energy die they use, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when your dice are all expended. You regain all your expended Spectral Energy dice when you finish a long rest.

In addition, when you reduce a hostile, enemy creature to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to channel their fleeting vitality into yourself, regaining one expended Spectral Energy die. You can regain a number of Spectral Energy dice this way equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.
When you reach certain levels in this class, the size of your Spectral Energy dice increases: at 5th level ({@dice d8}), 11th level ({@dice d10}), and 17th level ({@dice d12}).
The powers below use your Spectral Energy Dice.

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Slash
entries: When you make an attack roll against a creature, you can imbue your strike with ghastly necrotic energy. Expend one Spectral Energy die, and add the number you rolled to your attack and damage rolls of this attack. The extra damage dealt by this ability is necrotic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Ghost Barrier
entries: As a reaction, when you are hit by an attack, you can expend one Spectral Energy die and gain AC equal to that roll until the start of your next turn, potentially turning a hit into a miss.

subclassFeature.name: Invoke Terror
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend one Spectral Energy die to cause your form to crackle with necrotic energy. All creatures of your choice within 15ft must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + Proficiency Bonus) or become {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Merciless
entries: Also starting at 3rd level, you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures who are {@condition frightened}.

subclassFeature.name: One With The Fallen
entries: Starting at 7th level, you unlock new Spectral abilities.

subclassFeature.name: Vanishment
entries: You unlock the power to turn intangible for a short time. As an action, you and all objects you are wearing and carrying become spectral in form, and you can move through objects and other creatures as though they were difficult terrain. While in this form, you resist all damage except force damage. This transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you attack, cast a spell, or force a creature to make a saving throw. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again unless you expend one Spectral Energy die.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Guidance
entries: As a reaction, immediately after you fail a Strength, Constitution or Charisma saving throw, you can roll a Spectral Energy die and add that result to the total, potentially turning failure into success. If you still fail that saving throw, your Spectral Energy die is not expended by using this ability.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Command
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can cast the spell {@spell Animate Dead} without requiring material components, and its casting time is reduced to 1 action when you cast it using this feature.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ectoplasmic
entries: At 15th level, you gain the strength to expand your necrotic powers beyond your form. As a bonus action, you cause your form to glow, shedding dim green light in a 30ft radius for the next minute.
Other creatures of your choice within the light have advantage on Constitution and Death saving throws, and gain temporary hit points equal to your constitution modifier at the start of their turns.
Once you take this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a Spectral Energy die to do it again.

subclassFeature.name: From Beyond
entries: At 18th level, when you fall to 0 hit points, your spirit can leave your unconscious form and continue to fight. You appear as a translucent, white shade of your living self, complete with your equipment.
While in this form your statistics remain the same, but the only actions you can take on your turn are the help action and the attack action.
In addition, whenever you make a Death saving throw, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
You cannot cast spells or manipulate objects in this form, and you are immune to poison, cold, and necrotic damage. In addition, your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage.
Any damage dealt to your spirit form or your unconscious body causes a failed death saving throw as usual.
You can remain in spirit form for upto 10 minutes, or until your body regains consciousness, or you die, at which time your spirit form instantly vanishes.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you complete a long rest.

race.name: Castanoot
entries: There are three main variants: The {@race Castanoot (Caescean)|DMSecretWeapon|Caescean}, {@race Castanoot (Dentata)|DMSecretWeapon|Dentata}, and {@race Castanoot (Sativan)|DMSecretWeapon|Sativan}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Most Zu-Zoi stand a little shorter than a typical human, at around 5 feet. Your size is Medium.

entries.name: Age
entries: Zu-Zoi have shorter lifespans than humans, laying eggs that hatch and mature in a single year, and go on to live for roughly half a century. They show few internal or external signs of age, as healthy and intelligent in their second year as in their last.

entries.name: Many Eyes
entries: You gain proficiency in either {@skill Insight} or {@skill Perception} (your choice).

entries.name: One with the Land
entries: You gain proficiency in either {@skill Nature} or {@skill Survival} (your choice).

entries.name: Steadfast Spirit
entries: You have advantage on saving throws to resist {@condition exhaustion}.

sizeEntry.name: Small:
entries: Feytroll are around 3 feet tall and weigh between 50-60 pounds. Your size is Small.

entries.name: Age
entries: New Feytroll are born from the earth after two fully matured Feytroll engage in a magical courtship ritual under the gentle glow of dawn's first light, while both the sun and moon share the sky. They grow to adulthood over the course of 30 years, and then go on to live for several centuries.

entries.name: Fey
entries: Your creature type is Fey, rather than humanoid.

entries.name: Woodland Being
entries: You have proficiency in one of the following skills: {@skill Stealth}, {@skill Animal Handling}, or {@skill Nature}.

entries.name: Sunborn
entries: You can spend 10 minutes bathing in the light of the sun. If you do, you gain the benefits of a short rest. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Moonborn
entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern colour in darkness, only shades of grey.

entries.name: Natural Illusionist
entries: You know the {@spell minor illusion} cantrip. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the spell {@spell disguise self} without components with this trait. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast the spell {@spell invisibility} without components with this trait. Once you cast {@spell disguise self} or {@spell invisibility} with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this race).

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Lostanta vary widely in height and build, from barely 5 feet to well over 6 feet tall. Regardless of your position in that range, your size is Medium.

entries.name: Age
entries: Lostanta age incredibly slowly, reaching physical maturity after about 50 years, and going on to live for up to a millenia.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Lostanta are as variable in character as any other humanoid, but generations in the Ethereal Plane have shifted their outlook towards an apathetic, distant view of morality. They tend towards Neutral alignment.

entries.name: Timeless
entries: You have advantage on Constitution saves to resist the {@condition exhaustion} condition.

entries.name: Long Lived
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill History} and {@skill Survival} skills.

entries.name: Born of the Void
entries: You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as though it were bright light, and in darkness as though it were dim light. In addition, you can use a bonus action to focus your ethereal powers and grant yourself 10 ft. of blindsight until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Ancient Training
entries: You learn a {@filter fighting style|optionalfeatures|Feature Type=FS:F} of your choice from the fighter class, or you learn a {@filter cantrip|spells|class=sorcerer|level=0} of your choice from the sorcerer class. Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this race).

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: The typical Cyclod adult stands around 7ft tall. Your size is Medium.

entries.name: Longstriders
entries: Your base walking speed is 35 ft.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

entries.name: Natural Aptitude
entries: You gain proficiency with one tool, one skill, and one martial weapon of your choice.

entries.name: Magic Eye
entries: You can see up to 500 ft. away without difficulty, able to discern even fine details as though looking at something no more than 100 feet away from you. In addition, you can see in dim light within 120 ft. of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

entries.name: Cyclod Regeneration
entries: As a bonus action, you can spend one hit die to heal yourself. Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum of 1). You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: You are the same size as your original race, or your size can be Medium or Small.

entries.name: Clagborne Traits
entries: Clagborne are formed by a brainless ooze melding with a humanoid corpse. You may choose the humanoid race your Clagborne melded with, and use some of its statistics in your stat block. At your DMs discretion, you may become a Clagborne after your player character dies and melds with the ooze.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write any languages your original race knew in life, or you can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 30 feet. Even if your base race had a natural flying or swimming speed, you do not.

entries.name: Unusual Nature
entries: You don't need to breathe and you do not age.

entries.name: Clagborne Legacy
entries: If you replace a race with this lineage, you can retain any skill proficiencies you gained from it. If not, you gain proficiency in two skills of your choice. In addition, if your original race could take a feat with a racial prerequisite, you can still take it as a Clagborne.

entries.name: Ooze
entries: You have a climb speed equal to your walking speed, and can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: While you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 13 + your Constitution modifier. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

entries.name: Malleable Form
entries: You can move through the space of any creature that is of a size equal to or larger than yours.

entries.name: Translucency
entries: As a bonus action, you can alter the translucency of your ooze body, potentially frightening an enemy by revealing the skeleton within. When you do so, one creature of your choice with 15 ft. who can see you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus) or become {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries: Whenever you roll a hit dice to recover hit points, treat any number rolled on that dice as the maximum. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries.name: Age
entries: You do not age. Westurai are created fully formed, and have no concept of childhood, youth, or old age.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Westurai tend towards lawful good alignments, but those free of their creator's influence may drift towards more neutral and chaotic outlooks.

entries.name: Speed
entries: You have a base walking speed of 30ft, and a flying speed equal to your walking speed. In order to sustain your heavy body in flight, you require maximum maneuverability. You can't fly while wearing medium or heavy armor.

entries.name: From Stone
entries: Your body was hewn from stone before being imbued with magic. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 12 + your Constitution modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

entries.name: Stone Form
entries: As an action, you can shift into a being of pure stone. You and all objects you are holding turn to stone. Your movement speed becomes 0, attack rolls against you are made at advantage, and you auto fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws. In addition, you resist all damage, you have advantage on Constitution and Wisdom saving throws, and you can't take any actions, except to use an action to return to normal. You are indistinguishable from a true statue. Only a creature who succeeds on an Investigation check ({@dc 13}) can identify you as a Westurai.

entries.name: Divine Impetus
entries: You have advantage on saving throws to resist the {@condition charmed} condition, and you gain proficiency in the {@skill Religion} skill.

entries.name: Divine Magic
entries: You know the {@spell mending} cantrip. Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell sanctuary} spell with his trait. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast the {@spell calm emotions} spell with this trait. Once you cast {@spell sanctuary} or {@spell calm emotions} with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells when you cast them with this trait (choose when you select this race).

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Aemyr stand between 2 and 3ft tall. Your size is Small.

entries.name: Age
entries: Aemyr mature slower than humans, reaching adulthood in their third decade. On average, they live for about 80 years.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your base walking speed is 30ft, and you have a fly speed equal to your walking speed while you aren't wearing medium or heavy armour.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Ichorborne vary wildly in size, from as small as 3 feet all the way up to 8 feet tall. Your size is Medium or Small.

entries.name: Age
entries: Ichorborne come into being at sites of great bloodshed. They have no childhood and show no signs of ageing. Their bodies last roughly a century before breaking down.

entries.name: Ichoral Intuition
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine} skill.

entries.name: Humoural Tampering
entries: Once per turn, when you come into physical contact with a creature, you can force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, that creature is {@condition poisoned} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Bloodmist
entries: As an action, you can shift your form and any everything you are wearing and carrying into a misty cloud of red vapour.

While in this form, your only method of movement is a flying speed of 10 ft. You can enter and occupy the space of another creature. You resist nonmagical damage, and can pass through small holes, narrow openings, and even mere cracks, but you treat liquids as though they were solid surfaces. While in this form you can't fall, and remain hovering in the air even when {@condition stunned} or otherwise {@condition incapacitated}.
While in Bloodmist form, you can't talk or manipulate objects, and any objects you were carrying or holding can't be dropped, used, or otherwise interacted with. You can't attack or cast spells.

This transformation lasts for 10 minutes, or until you use a bonus action to end it. It ends early if you are knocked {@condition unconscious}. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Neutral, Lawful

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: You have a thick, spiky hide. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 12 + your Constitution modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

entries.name: Wardens
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Nature} skill.

entries.name: Spiny Shell
entries: You may use your reaction to lean into your thick, spiny shell. Until the end of this turn, you gain advantage on Constitution saving throws. You may use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries.name: Greatberry
entries: You know the {@spell druidcraft} cantrip. Starting at 3rd level, you may also cast {@spell goodberry} once per long rest using this trait. Any {@spell goodberry} created using this trait is a Greatberry, and restores hit points equal to 1 + your proficiency modifier.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Lawful, Good

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: You have a thick, spiky hide. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 12 + your Constitution modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.

entries.name: Survivalist
entries: You are proficient in the {@skill Survival} skill.

entries.name: Spikey Shell
entries: When a creature within 5 ft. hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal piercing damage equal to your Constitution modifier to that creature. From level 6, the earthen power imbued in your shell has grown to the extent that this counts as magical damage for the purposes of overcoming resistances. From level 11, your skill at maximising your shell offensively allows you to add your proficiency modifier to any damage dealt with this trait.

entries.name: Tumbler
entries: You can use a reaction to halve any fall damage you would take. You may use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Chaotic, Good

entries.name: Rolliking Spirit
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill.

entries.name: Vigorous Energy
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition stunned} or {@condition paralyzed}.

entries.name: Quick Footed
entries: Your base walking speed is 35 ft.

entries.name: Stop, Drop and Roll
entries: When you are dealt damage, you can use a reaction to fall {@condition prone} and move 35 ft. in any direction along the ground in a straight line. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a short or a long rest.

entries.name: Venom Blood
entries: You have resistance to poison damage and are immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition.

entries.name: Living Weapon
entries: As a bonus action, you can coat a single piercing or slashing melee weapon you are holding with your natural venom. Once applied, this venom remains potent for the next minute, or until the weapon hits another creature. A creature hit by this weapon must make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or take an additional {@damage 1d10} poison damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d10} at level 5, {@damage 3d10} at level 11, and {@damage 4d10} at level 17. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier per long rest.

entries.name: Hard Earned Freedom
entries: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.

entries.name: Adaptive Carapice
entries: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to grant yourself resistance to that damage type for the next minute. Once you use this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a short rest.

entries.name: Hasty Response
entries: You have advantage on initiative rolls.

entries.name: Strong of Heart
entries: You have advantage on Charisma saving throws.

entries.name: Forest Dweller
entries: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice from among {@skill Nature}, {@skill Survival}, {@skill Perception} and {@skill Animal Handling}.

entries.name: Flaxfoot Magic
entries: You know the {@spell dancing lights} cantrip, and can choose to cast it without verbal or somatic components a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries.name: Lowstone Resistance
entries: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition poisoned} condition, and you resist poison damage.

entries.name: Strength of Mind
entries: You have advantage on Intelligence saving throws.

entries.name: Sturdy Wings
entries: You can fly while wearing medium armour.

entries.name: Mountain Dweller
entries: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice from among {@skill Nature}, {@skill Athletics}, {@skill Medicine} and {@skill Insight}.

entries.name: Lowstone Magic
entries: You know the {@spell mending} cantrip, and can choose to cast it with a casting time of one action, rather than one minute, a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

raceFluff.name: Castanoot
entries: Castanoot are a race of small, fey creatures native to the feywild who are notable for their thick, spined shells. An ancient and deeply solitary peoples, Castanoot are famously distrustful of outsiders and seek to avoid interaction with others if they can. However, they have been known to trade and associate with other races on occasion. Trust is hard earned however, and easily lost. Castanoot have a strong distrust of Fairies for an insult dealt unto them long ago that none remember, aside from the fact it came from the tongue of a Fairy.

Although Castanoot can burrow, they typically live in woodland areas, building homes inside trees. They age rapidly from birth, reaching adulthood in just 5 years, and then go on to live for around a century.

items.name: Caescean
entries: Caescean Castanoot are the most traditionally focused of all Castanoot races. They live in tight knit, matriarchal societies on lands claimed long ago. They take great pride in their heritage, and resist change fiercely.

items.name: Dentata
entries: The Dentata Castanoot are a warrior people. They find great joy in hunting as a tribe and combative sports. To the Dentata, a Castanoot's shell is of the utmost importance, and many hours each day are devoted to the cleaning, decoration and preservation of one's shell. It is their first line of defence, and most trusted weapon.

items.name: Sativan
entries: The Sativan Castanoot are a nomadic people who long ago cast off their spiky shells and the traditions of the old ways in favour of physical and social mobility. They shirk the isolationist philosophies of other Castanoot and traverse the feywild, delighting in meeting new creatures. They are famous for living in open, polyamerous societies, although finding two Sativan committed exclusively to one another is not uncommon.

raceFluff.name: Zu-Zoi
entries: The Zu-Zoi are a jungle dwelling species of sentient, insectoid humanoids. Once a slave-race, Zu-Zoi are intensely aggressive and territorial, having learned to fear and despise outsiders.

They trade with other species only as a necessity, as they lack the resources and knowledge to produce complex mechanical or magical objects. However, they are not primitive. Zu-Zoi are beyond virtuosic in the fields of agriculture, survivalism and combat.
It's said Zu-Zoi can turn a barren wasteland to a thriving, luscious forest in a single generation.
There are two primary subraces which co-exist peacefully: the {@race Zu-Zoi (Zat)|DMSecretWeapon|Zu-Zoi-Zat} and {@race Zu-Zoi (Zen)|DMSecretWeapon|Zu-Zoi-Zen}.

raceFluff.name: Feytroll
entries: Feytroll are a race of small, solitary creatures native to the forests of the material plane. Zealous collectors, most Feytroll adore shiny objects, regardless of their financial worth, and use them to decorate their nests and clothing. Usually fearful of larger creatures, Feytroll typically protect themselves with illusion magic, choosing to hide away rather than engage with other beings. Brave or curious Feytroll who seek to explore the world and socialise are not unheard of, however.

All Feytroll feel a deep connection with the sun and moon, with many choosing to actively worship the heavenly spheres. Names such as Solus, Dusk, Dawn, Luna, Fireborn, Brightborn, Wolfmoon, and Helios are common among Feytroll.

raceFluff.name: Lostanta
entries: Lostanta are fallen humans native to the Ethereal Plane. Originally a nation of proud and ambitious people, the Lostanta sought to replicate the long life of elves, infusing themselves with youth, power and beauty beyond their natural limitations.

In punishment for transgressions against their true nature, they were banished from the material plane, left in a timeless void where they barely age or tire. Some have found ways back to their ancient home, and wander the material plane mourning that which their people left behind in pursuit of immortality.

raceFluff.name: Cyclod
entries: The Cyclod are a reclusive race of fey, distant descendants of the mighty Titans. Easily identifiable by the single, large eye in the center of their head and their large tusks, their imposing appearance and scarcity have led to Cyclods being vilified in many cultures as bestial monsters that consume humanoid flesh.

In actuality, they are a gentle and timid people, forming small, nomadic communities of roughly a dozen families who wander the mountains of the material plane. No two Cyclods share the same colouration of skin, each born with their own unique coloration and patterns. Cyclod elders traditionally interpret these patterns to predict a newborn's future.

raceFluff.name: Clagborne Lineage
entries: A peculiar species of subterranean magical ooze, Clagborne are a deeply mysterious race. Unique in that they are fully amorphous and brainless until they find a host, almost nothing is known of a Clagborne's early life or origin, as even they remember nothing of it.

What is known is that these brainless oozes slime their way through caverns and dungeons on instinct, until they come upon a humanoid corpse. At this point, the Clagborne strips the body of its flesh and tissue, magically absorbing all chemical and electrical information, and is “born” as a new entity, complete with all the memories of its fallen host.
The ooze wraps around the skeleton, forming a new body in the model of the old. A Clagborne can alter the transparency and colour of its slime flesh to suit its wishes.

Although a Clagborne retains the memories their original form had in life and are functionally identical in personality, desires and ability, they are a distinct creature. The soul of the departed does not return to the Clagborne, and many struggle coming to terms with their identity.
Are they the same person as they were in life? Or an abominable walking undead, host to a parasitic, brainless monster?

raceFluff.name: Westurai
entries: Created by Celestial Gods to articulate their designs on the material plane, Westurai are a mysterious, enigmatic race devoted entirely to their divine purpose.

Each is magically hewn from stone with a fully formed mind and impetus. Be it to guard a temple, gather information, destroy evil, or explore the world, most Westurai have their actions dictated to the letter by the god who created them. They obey these orders unthinkingly and without passion.

However, should their orders cease to arrive, perhaps through the death of a god or a severing of the divine connection, a Westurai becomes free to act independently, forging their own destiny as a living being.

raceFluff.name: Aemyr
entries: Ancient legends tell that the first Aemyr were created by a powerful, empathetic archfey who sought to create guardians for the natural world across all planes of existence. Aemyr have been found on many planes, uniquely adapted to suit their environment. There are two primary subraces that exist on the Material Plane: The {@race Aemyr (Flaxfoot)|DMSecretWeapon|Flaxfoot Aemyr} and The {@race Aemyr (Lowstone)|DMSecretWeapon|Lowstone Aemyr}.

items.name: Flaxfoot
entries: Flaxfoot Aemyr usually dwell in forests, and by natural disposition are playful and merry. They have an unfortunate reputation for gluttony, and overindulgence in fine food and drink, however this is largely unfounded. Flaxfoot enjoy the bounties of their forest home to the fullest, but they are no more greedy or gluttonous than any other race. Still, rarely do travellers who come upon a Flaxfoot town leave the next morning without a full belly and ringing hangover.

items.name: Lowstone
entries: Lowstone Aemyr are mountain dwellers. Acclimated to life at the very peak of the tallest mountains, they are a rare sight on the lands below. Many Mountain Dwarf legends feature Lowstone as invisible protectors or guardians to those who fall foul of the mountain. They are rumoured to have the power to sense volcanic eruptions and earthquakes before they happen, and have long aided Dwarves building mighty mountain fortresses in ways that will not provoke the mountain's wrath.

raceFluff.name: Ichorborne
entries: Legends tell of the Ichorborne, a cursed race hewn from dark magic. Walking abominations, held together without skin or sinew; a swirling mist of blood and terror. They take humanoid form, with crimson flesh and scent of iron. The air about them ripples with the taste of blood. These are the tales the people tell.

As sentient and capable of goodness as any other race, the Ichorborne are so rare, and so feared, they struggle to find acceptance in the wider world. Formed from the memories of innocents whose blood has been shed, they emerge into the world fully formed and sentient. A chaotic amalgamation of personalities bound to a single mind.

Many Ichorborne isolate themselves entirely, or disguise themselves as hooded, masked travellers, attempting to live a quiet existence among the rest of the world. Some seek vengeance on those who harm the innocent. Unless an individual can somehow prove themselves to a community and receive acceptance, the life of the Ichorborne is forever one of suspicion, persecution, and secrecy.

trait.name: Shapechanger
entries: The mimicule can use its action to polymorph into a tiny object or back into its true, amorphous form. Its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: Adhesive (Object Form Only)
entries: The mimicule can choose to adhere to anything that touches it. A Medium or smaller creature adhered to the mimicule is also {@condition grappled} by it (escape {@dc 10}). Ability checks made to escape this grapple have disadvantage.

trait.name: False Appearance (Object Form Only)
entries: While the mimicule remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary object.

action.name: Bite

trait.name: Blessing of Hammurabi
entries: The whydra cannot be damaged or affected by any creature more than 10 ft. away from it. It is immune to any spell or other magical effect created by a creature for as long as that creature is more than 10 ft. away.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
entries: If the whydra fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magical Resistance
entries: The whydra has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Colossal Tangle
entries: The whydra is a frenzied mass of ever biting heads. Due to its immense size and lack of precision, whenever it attacks a creature and misses, that creature must make a {@dc 19} Dexterity saving throw (they can choose to fail) or else be knocked 30 ft. away from the whydra, taking 28 ({@damage 8d6}) bludgeoning damage and falling {@condition prone}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The whydra can make any number of bite attacks a turn.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +18} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}14 ({@damage 1d10 + 9}) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Always On Guard
entries: The whydra can make a single bite attack as a reaction whenever another creature moves or appears within 20 ft. of it.

action.name: Club
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +2} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4}) bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The mechanical spider can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Limited Nanite Regeneration
entries: When the mechanical spider is reduced to 0 hit points, self-contained nanomachines automatically repair some of the damage, returning it to 1 hit point instead. This feature can only be used once per day.

action.name: Foreleg
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage.

action.name: Synthetic Web {@recharge 5}
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +5} to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. {@h}The target is {@condition restrained} by webbing. As an action, the restrained target can make a {@dc 12} Strength check, bursting the webbing on a success. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; hp 5; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).

trait.name: Enigmatic Origin
entries: The Invader's speech is impossible to decipher even with the use of magic. Its equipment is beyond the understanding of anyone of this world and cannot be used by them.

trait.name: Disintegration Ray
entries: Any creature that is reduced to 0 hit points by the Invader's Raygun is instantly killed and reduced to a pile of ash.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the Invader fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Invader makes two Raygun attacks.

action.name: Raygun
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +6} to hit, range 60/180 ft., 1 target. {@h}18 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) fire damage.

action.name: OVERCHARGE {@recharge 5}
entries: The Invader fires a beam in a 60-foot line that is 5 feet wide from its Raygun. All creatures in the line must make a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw taking 22 ({@damage 5d8}) fire damage on a failed save and half as much on a successful one.

legendary.name: Holograms! (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The Invader creates 2 Hologram copies of itself which appear in two unoccupied spaces it can see within 30 ft. They have a walking speed of 30 ft., AC 10, and disappear if they are dealt any damage or are more than 30 ft. from The Invader at the start of its turn. When the invader attacks, all the holograms attack simultaneously, targeting the same creature (the holograms do no damage).

legendary.name: Hologram Swap
entries: The Invader can switch places with one of its holograms. This switch is not discernible to other creatures.

trait.name: Necrotic Touch
entries: When the necrotic elemental hits a creature, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or have its hit point maximum reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. The target dies if this attack reduces its hit point maximum to 0. The reduction lasts until the target completes a long rest or is removed by the {@spell greater restoration} spell or other magic.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The elemental makes two touch attacks.

action.name: Touch
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +8} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) necrotic damage.

action.name: Necroshade {@recharge 4}
entries: Each creature within 10 ft. of the elemental must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a target takes 14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) necrotic damage and is {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Psychic Aura
entries: Any creature who targets the elemental with an attack or harmful spell must first make a {@dc 13} Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature must choose a new target or lose the attack or spell. This ability doesn't protect the elemental from area effects, such as the explosion of a {@spell fireball}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The elemental makes two beam attacks.

action.name: Beam
entries: The psychic elemental shoots a beam at a creature it can see within 60 ft. of it. That target makes a {@dc 16} Intelligence saving throw, taking 14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) psychic damage on a failed save.

action.name: Apathy Blast {@recharge 4}
entries: Each creature within 10 ft. of the elemental must make a {@dc 16} Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, they forget the elemental exists, it becomes {@condition invisible} to them, and the concept of its existence cannot form in their mind. This effect ends if the elemental attacks that creature, or they take damage.

trait.name: Radiant Blast
entries: Whenever the elemental is damaged by an attack or harmful spell, all creatures of the elemental's choice within 15 ft. of it must make a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The elemental makes two slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +8} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) radiant damage.

action.name: Radiant Glow {@recharge 4}
entries: A 10-ft. radius, 40 ft. high beam of light shines down on a point of the elemental's choice within 60 ft. of it. Each creature in the light regains 9 ({@damage 1d8 + 5}) hit points. If a creature at full hit points would gain the benefit of this effect, they regain 9 ({@damage 1d8 + 5}) temporary hit points instead.

trait.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces the Undead guard to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the Undead guard drops to 1 hit point instead. This ability can only be used once per long rest.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The undead guard makes two melee attacks.

action.name: Scimitar
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) slashing damage.

trait.name: Unusual Nature
entries: The skeleton giant doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If the skeleton giant fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The skeleton makes two greataxe attacks. It can replace one of these attacks with its Enervating Stare.

action.name: Greataxe
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +9} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}25 ({@damage 3d12 + 6}) slashing damage.

action.name: Enervating Stare
entries: The skeleton targets one creature it can see within 60 feet of it. The target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or take 35 ({@damage 10d6}) necrotic damage.

monster.name: Poison Mummy
languages: the languages it knew in life

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The poison mummy uses its Poison Blast and then makes one attack with its Rotting Fist.

action.name: Rotting Fist
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) bludgeoning damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be cursed with mummy rot. The cursed target can't regain hit points, and its hit point maximum decreases by 10 ({@damage 3d6}) for every 24 hours that elapse. If the curse reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and its body turns to dust. The curse lasts until removed by the {@spell remove curse} spell or other magic.

action.name: Poison Blast
entries: The mummy targets one creature it can see within 30 feet. A jet of poisonous bile shoots towards the creature. It must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw against the blast or become {@condition poisoned} until the end of the poison mummy's next turn. If the target fails the saving throw by 5 or more, it also takes 22 ({@damage 5d8}) poison damage.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The High Priestess' innate spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save {@dc 17}, {@hit +7} to hit with spell attacks). She can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components:

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The High Priestess has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The High Priestess makes two attacks: one with its longsword and one with its shortsword.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) slashing damage.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) piercing damage.

trait.name: Tunneler
entries: The wormling can burrow through solid rock at half its burrow speed and leaves a 1-foot-diameter tunnel in its wake.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wormling makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its stinger.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) piercing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) acid damage.

action.name: Tail Stinger
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) piercing damage plus 21 ({@damage 6d6}) poison damage. The target must make a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw, taking the poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

monster.name: Kraken Hatchling
languages: understands Abyssal, Celestial, Infernal, and Primordial but can't speak

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The kraken can breathe air and water.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The kraken makes three attacks between its tentacles and lightning shock.

action.name: Tentacle
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +8} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d6 + 5}) bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature it is {@condition grappled} (escape {@dc 14}). Until this grapple ends, the target is {@condition restrained}. The Kraken Hatchling has 10 tentacles, each of which can grapple one target.

action.name: Lightning Shock
entries: The Kraken Hatchling magically charges a burst of lightning through its body. All creatures it is touching must make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw, taking 22 ({@damage 4d10}) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. Creatures submerged in water make this save at disadvantage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Blood Demon makes two Claw attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of its Vomit Blood ability.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8}) slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) acid damage.

action.name: Vomit Blood {@recharge 5}
entries: The Blood Demon vomits acidic blood in a 30-foot line 5 feet wide. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw or take 14 ({@damage 4d6}) acid damage or half as much damage on a successful save.

resist.note: from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered

trait.name: Abyssal Weapons
entries: Xer'Gaal's weapon attacks are magical and deal an extra 13 ({@damage 3d8}) necrotic damage on a hit (included in the attacks).

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: Xer'Gaal has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

bonus.name: Incorporeal Form
entries: Xer'Gaal turns {@condition invisible} and incorporeal until the start of its next turn. In this form, it resists all damage except force and radiant damage, and can move through creatures and objects as though they were difficult terrain. It takes {@damage 1d10} force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Once Xer'Gaal uses this feature, it cannot do so again until it reduces another creature to 0 hit points.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Xer'Gaal makes three attacks.

action.name: Longsword +2
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +11} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8}) slashing damage, or 9 ({@damage 1d10}) slashing damage if used with two hands, plus 13 ({@damage 3d8}) necrotic damage.

action.name: Blood Storm {@recharge 5}
entries: Xer'Gaal conjures a storm of blood to rain in a 20-foot-radius sphere centred on a point Xer'Gaal can see within 120 feet of it. The sphere remains for 1 minute or until Xer'Gaal loses {@status concentration} (as if concentrating on a spell), and its area is lightly obscured and difficult terrain.

Any creature that moves into the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw. A creature takes 16 ({@damage 3d10}) acid damage plus 16 ({@damage 3d10}) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Any corpses caught in the area are turned into Blood Demons.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: Xer'Gaal adds 4 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, Xer'Gaal must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

legendary.name: Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Xer'Gaal makes a longsword attack.

legendary.name: Move
entries: Xer'Gaal moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The Tarrasque Pup has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Hardened Carapace
