table.name: NPC Quirks
intro: Coming up with a quick quirk for an NPC is a powerful way of keeping them memorable for your players, and giving yourself a simple "in" when improvising and interacting with them. You can use this table to roll randomly and determine a quick trait to breathe some life into your NPCs, or choose any quirks that inspire you.
rows: Is instantly infatuated with a player character
Is convinced they are dead
Has two eyes of different colors that switch when they blink
Is covered in tattoos that glow and subtly move around
Permanently radiates a faint scent of urine, due to a fey curse
Is constantly eating, yet extremely skinny
Smokes an enormous and ornate pipe, blowing billowing smoke over the party
Constantly bounces on the balls of their feet, forever in motion
Believes themselves to be incredibly important and famous
Is always extremely tired and bored, even when discussing exciting events
Is obsessed with fashion, commenting on and suggesting improvements for the party's aesthetic
Begins to float into the air unsupported when aggravated or excited
Is a fantastic pickpocket, often taking party items without their knowledge only to hand the stolen goods back to them
Is surrounded by animals at all times, much to their frustration
Is extremely nervous and shy
Is extremely extroverted and confident, and accentuates their words with bursts of magical light and showers of sparks
Dresses all in one color, and decorates their shop, home and pets the same
Is extremely forgetful, calling PCs by the incorrect name and losing the thread of details quickly
Is extremely sensitive to sunlight, stays fully cloaked and lurks in darkness
Is appalling messy, leaving a trail of garbage behind them wherever they go
Says the phrase "Gotta Live, Gotta Laugh, Gotta Love" way too much
Asks PCs deeply personal questions with no warning
100% believes any conspiracy theory at once; the less evidence, the better
Is convinced the world will end within the next 12 months, but is not sure how
Is suicidally brave and daring
Is an obsessive gambler, and will attempt to draw the party into games of chance for gold
Is three kobolds in a trenchcoat, attempting to pass as a dragonborn, and will deny any accusations to the contrary
Is surrounded by floating motes of golden light
Is a changeling who shifts appearance to mimic the exact look of whoever is addressing them
Is a druid who keeps accidentally transforming into a golden retriever whenever they sneeze

table.name: The Chaos Dice Wild Magic Table of Time and Space
intro: This extended Wild Magic table is useful for quickly determining interesting and varied surges of Wild Magic. You might also wish to roll randomly or choose an effect to act as a curse or boon attached to a magical weapon. Some effects will work well as offensive magical powers, perfect for spicing up a mighty, homebrewed monster.

They have been designed to not be overly debilitating, carrying little risk of a T.P.K., or game breaking benefit. This answers a serious issue I've had with other Wild Magic tables, which have the potential to end games on the spot! This one is appropriate for players and games of any level. Now come with us on a journey through time and space!
All effects end on a long rest, unless specified otherwise.
rows: Roll twice on this table, ignoring this result.
You grow {@dice 1d10} years younger, but no younger than 9 years old.
You grow {@dice 1d10} years older, but no older than 99 years old.
Your skin and hair ages rapidly, giving you the appearance of an old hag. You have disadvantage on Charisma checks and advantage on Wisdom checks.

Any non-magical equipment you are carrying or wearing is ravaged by time; metal rusts and wood rots away. All weapons you are carrying become simple melee weapons that deal {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage on a hit, and armour you are wearing confers no benefit to you.
You gain a brief glimpse of the future. Make your next saving throw with advantage.

You are thrown through time. For you, a full hour of chaotic visions of different times pass through your mind before you once again land in the present. To everyone else, no time has passed. Take {@damage 4d8} psychic damage.
Your spirit is pushed back in time to before you woke up for the day. Regain one spent spell slot of third level or below.
A full 24 hours worth of time is poured into your body. Although no time passes, your body aches with weariness. You gain a level of exhaustion.
The spirit of a defeated enemy is wrenched through time and strikes at you. Take {@damage 4d4} necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum is reduced by the same amount.
A segment of time is removed from your history. You forget how you met your companions, although you still recognise them as allies.
Time unravels around you, sending your body to a previous time when it wasn't as well trained. You lose hit points equal to one roll of your hit die + your Constitution modifier.
The weave of time stretches around you. Your maximum lifespan is increased by {@dice 1d6} years. This effect does not wear off, even after a long rest.
The weave of time shrinks around you. Your maximum lifespan reduces by {@dice 1d6} years. This effect does not wear off, even after a long rest.
For you, time slows down. The next time you cast a spell with a casting time of one action, you can cast it using a bonus action instead.

To you, others seem to speed up. Those around you move and talk faster and are hard to keep up with. Your maximum speed reduces by 10ft, and you take a -2 penalty to Dexterity saving throws and your AC.
You are pulled more in focus with the magic of the time stream, gaining an element of precognition. The next time you roll for initiative, roll with advantage.
Your spirit is shunted forward in time to a point after the strains of the battle to come. You lose {@damage 2d6} hit points and one 3rd level spell slot.

You see a glimpse of your own, natural death. At your DM's discretion, you know the exact date and time you would die, if left to natural causes. You can still die in other ways and at other times, or extend your life beyond that point with magic if you choose to seek means to do so.

You obtain a small Time Stone Fragment that orbits your head. It contains a single charge. As an action, you can expend its charge to cast the spell {@spell time stop} without any components, and the Fragment crumbles to dust.

You and everything you are wearing or carrying increase in size by one size category. You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your weapon attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d4} damage.

You and everything you are wearing or carrying shrink by one size category. You have disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your weapon attacks deal {@damage 1d4} less damage (but no less than 1).
You magically teleport to an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you on the ground.
One body part of your choice grows in size by 3 inches. You can choose for this benefit not to end, even after a long rest.
Your firm connection to this plane of existence is shaken. You gain the benefits of the {@spell blink} spell for its full duration.

A single object you are carrying grows steadily heavier over the course of the next six seconds until it is too heavy to hold. You drop the object, and it remains immovable on the ground for the next minute.

You become lighter than air. You rise vertically 20ft in the air at the end of each of your turns. On your turns, you can move vertically up or down as part of your normal movement speed. You cannot move horizontally while in the air, unless you push or pull yourself against a fixed object or surface within reach.
Your head and any headgear you are wearing swells to twice its natural size.
Your body grows incredibly heavy. Your walking speed reduces by 10ft, you lose any flying speed, and you have advantage on Strength-based ability checks and saving throws.
You are banished to a heavenly plane of existence until the end of your next turn. While there, you bask in the warmth and energy of the plane, gaining the benefits of a short rest.
You are banished to a terrifying plane of darkness until the end of your next turn. The oppressive blackness strikes at your mind. You gain a level of exhaustion upon your return.
Your body shifts into an identical copy of a random creature you can see. Your statistics and abilities remain the same.
A blast of spatial energy ripples forth from you. All creatures within 100ft of you are knocked {@condition prone}.

The space around you twists and writhes, bending to your whim. You have advantage on attack rolls against creatures within 5ft of you, and score a critical hit on a 19 or a 20 for the next 10 minutes.
The space around you inverts, flipping everything upside down. You make attack rolls at disadvantage. This effect ends after 10 minutes.

A random person you know is wrenched through space and appears within 5ft of you. They act according to their alignment and relationship with you for the next minute before being teleported back to where they came from.
Light bends around your form. You are {@condition invisible} and {@condition blinded} for the next minute.
The inky blackness of the void bleeds out from your form. Magical darkness extends out from you in a 30ft radius for the next minute.
The air around you grows dense and thick as a crashing wave of gravitational pressure crushes you. You fall {@condition prone} and the effect ends.
The air is torn from your lungs as a bubble of void encases you. You cannot breathe and make no noise for the next minute.
The air around you thins into a low gravity field. Your jump distance is tripled.
The power to manipulate the space an object occupies surges through you. As an action, you can cast {@spell enlarge/reduce} without components or concentrating for the next minute.

You obtain a small Space Stone Fragment that orbits your head. It contains a single charge. As an action, you can expend its charge to cast the spell {@spell reverse gravity} without any components, and the Fragment crumbles to dust.
Time and Space warp the area around you. It's REALLY trippy. You vomit on the floor in front of you.
The space around you seems to grow thick, like stepping through molasses. Any creature other than you that moves within a 15ft radius of you must use 20ft of movement to travel 5ft.
You are frozen in place until the start of your next turn. You have immunity to all damage, are {@condition incapacitated}, and cannot move.
An inch thick forcefield of antigravity covers your body, working to push things away that move towards you. You float an inch off the floor, and your AC increases by 2 for the next minute.

You gain a personal gravity field, drawing small rocks and unfastened objects towards you. Your AC decreases by 2, and any ranged weapon attacks that pass within 10 feet of you shift target mid flight to strike you instead. This effect ends after 1 minute has passed.

A burst of gravitational energy funnels through you for the next minute. As an action, you can choose up to three creatures or objects that weigh less than 500lbs. You can move each up to 30ft in any direction, but creatures must end their movement on the ground.

A mote of endless possibility appears before you, and attempts to bind you with another creature of opposing energy nearby. Choose one effect on this table. You and one hostile creature within 60ft of you suffer the effect of your choice. If there is no hostile within 60ft of you, nothing happens.

table.name: Minor Weapon Boons
intro: None of these weapon boons directly deal extra damage. The idea here is to have a bunch of simple but exciting enhancements attached to weapons that add flavour and fun, not just some extra dice.
The minor weapon boons can be applied to any magic weapon at any level for flavour and cool points; they're not going to break the game.
rows: While attuned to this weapon, you can go up to seven times as long without needing food or drink.
Once you have attuned to this weapon, it can never be used to harm you, even if you unattune and it is wielded by someone else.
You can speak a command word to transform this weapon into a walking stick, or a functioning fishing rod, until you use the command word to transform it back.
While attuned to this weapon, you can understand and read {@language Sylvan}, or another language appropriate to the weapon's origin.
If you score a critical hit with this weapon, you can instantly teleport up to 15ft into an unoccupied space you can see.
While attuned to this weapon, your jump distance is tripled, and you take no fall damage from falling any distance smaller than your high jump.
Your reach while wielding this weapon is increased by 10ft, but you have disadvantage on attack rolls made using this weapon against enemies more than 5ft away.
If you speak a command word, this weapon sheds dim green light in a 15ft radius.
You have advantage on {@skill performance} checks that involve singing while you carry this weapon.
Whenever you roll a natural 1 while attacking with this weapon, you gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
If you hit a creature with this weapon on your turn, that creature cannot make an opportunity attack against you until the start of its next turn.
While attuned to this weapon, you have advantage on any skill check that involves interacting with beasts or creatures with an intelligence score of 3 or less.

Choose one willing creature you can see when you attune to this weapon. You can speak telepathically to that creature, although they may not understand you if you do not share a language, and they cannot communicate back telepathically.
While attuned to this weapon, you can cast the spell {@spell prestidigitation} without components once per short rest.
This weapon is invisible to anyone besides you while you are carrying it on your person.
Whenever you score a critical hit with this weapon, you can take the {@action Dodge} or {@action Help} action as a bonus action.
While attuned to this weapon, you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.
While attuned to this weapon, you can use your bonus action and 5ft of movement to escape a grapple. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
This weapon deals double damage to structures, objects and constructs.
Roll twice on this table, ignoring this result.

table.name: Major Weapon Boons
intro: The major weapon boons are serious business, I recommend saving those for important, quest-earned bonuses available to player characters of level 11+.
rows: Whenever you hit a creature with this weapon, you can teleport them up to 15ft into an unoccupied space that you can see.
While attuned to this weapon, your Strength score changes to 25, and you have advantage on Strength saving throws.
While attuned to this one-handed weapon, you gain proficiency with shields and all armour.

Whenever you roll a natural 1 when attacking with this weapon, it becomes a natural 20 instead. Once you use this feature, you gain a level of exhaustion and cannot use this trait again until you finish a long rest.

If you would fail a saving throw against a spell effect while attuned to this weapon, you can choose to lose hit points equal to that spell's level × 8. If you do so, you instead succeed on that saving throw.
You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed while attuned to this weapon. If you already have a flying speed, it is doubled for as long as you are attuned.

You can use an action to conjure up to 6 celestial spirits in the form of Griffons. They cannot attack or deal damage, and last for {@dice 2d6} hours. If they take any damage, they instantly vanish. If a Griffon vanishes while mounted, the rider descends at a controlled rate of 60ft a turn until they reach the ground, taking no fall damage. Once this trait has been used, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

Whenever you score a critical hit with this weapon, roll randomly on the {@table Minor Weapon Boons|DMSecretWeapon|Minor Weapon Boon} table. This weapon gains that benefit permanently. This ability can be triggered five times, after which no more boons can be added.

Whenever you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with this weapon, you can choose to reduce them to 1 hit point instead. If you do, that creature is {@condition charmed} by you, cannot attack you or your companions, and you have advantage on all social interactions with that creature for the next 24 hours.

When you first attune to this weapon, choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder damage. You have resistance to that damage type. If you are already resistant to that damage type from another source, you instead have immunity to that damage type.
You don't need to eat, sleep, or breathe, and you gain a swimming speed and climbing speed equal to your walking speed. In addition, you can complete a long rest in four hours of gentle activity.

If you score a critical hit with this weapon, you can choose to forgo rolling the extra damage dice to instead stun that creature until the start of your next turn. Once you use this trait, you cannot do so again until you complete a long or short rest.
You can add both your Strength and Dexterity modifiers to attack rolls made with this finesse weapon.

Whenever you score a critical hit with this weapon, you can use your bonus action to take the {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, interact with an object, or {@action Help} action, or make a single weapon attack.

This weapon gains the {@itemProperty T||thrown}, {@itemProperty L||light}, and {@itemProperty F||finesse} properties, with a range of 30/120ft. When you make a ranged attack with this weapon, you can use your Strength modifier when calculating attack and damage rolls. When you throw this weapon, it teleports back into your hand immediately after dealing damage or missing the target.
You do not need to eat, drink, or sleep, and you do not age. You also cannot be {@condition poisoned}, and are immune to all diseases.
As an action, you can cast {@spell alter self} through this weapon, without components. The spell lasts for the full duration without requiring concentration.

When you are hit with a melee attack, you can use a reaction to channel the vitality of this weapon and attempt to magically parry that blow. Add +6 to your AC against that one attack, potentially turning a hit into a miss. You must be able to see your attacker to activate this effect.

If you would be reduced to 0 hit points while attuned to this weapon, you are reduced to 1 hit point instead. You then gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier, and can use your reaction to immediately make a melee attack with this weapon. If you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
Roll twice on this table, ignoring this result.

variantrule.name: Zombification Station!
entries: What self-respecting DM hasn't had the occasional fantasy of setting a Zombie T-Rex on their players? How about a Zombie Kraken? A Zombie Hydra? A freakin' Zombie Tarrasque?!
By the same token, what self-respecting Player Character hasn't wanted all of the above as a pet?
Here you'll find a set of rules that you can apply to any creature to swiftly switch out its living incarnation into a terrifying, brain-devouring creature of the night!
Simply follow the base Zombie Conversion rules, and then choose any of the Zombie Boons or Zombie Penalties to add to your creature's stat block.
Choosing elements from the boons and penalties will allow you to tweak a creature's challenge rating and inject more "zombie" into your zombified creature.
The Superboss Zombie traits should be reserved for BBEGs only; they pack some serious wallop and will serve as a huge upgrade to any creature you hand them out to.

entries.name: Zombie Conversion Rules
entries: Here are the basic steps to convert a normal monster stat block to its zombified form:

items: Replace the creature type of your Zombified creature with Undead.
The creature gains immunity to poison damage and the {@condition poisoned} condition.
The creature gains resistance to necrotic damage.
The creature gains 60 feet of {@sense darkvision}. If it already has {@sense darkvision}, its range increases by 60 feet instead.

entries.name: Zombie Boons
entries: Here are various boons that you can grant your zombie to reflect its new undead power:

entries.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces this creature to 0 hit points, it makes a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the zombie drops to 1 hit point instead.

entries.name: Undead Persistence
entries: This creature is immune to the {@condition charmed}, {@condition exhaustion}, {@condition frightened}, and {@condition paralyzed} conditions.

entries.name: Magical Resistance
entries: This creature has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Undead Resistance
entries: This creature resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered.

entries.name: Cursed
entries: When this creature hits another creature with a melee weapon attack, that creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + Constitution modifier + proficiency bonus) or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
entries: This creature has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the zombie's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't {@condition incapacitated}.

entries.name: Bite Attack
entries: {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} Strength modifier + proficiency bonus to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@i Hit:} {@dice 1d8} + Strength modifier damage, plus {@damage 2d8} necrotic damage.

entries.name: Zombie Penalties
entries: Here are some downsides you can add to your zombies for flavour and tangible mechanical ramifications:

entries.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries: While in sunlight, this creature has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Unholy
entries: This creature is vulnerable to radiant damage.

entries.name: Shambling Walker
entries: This creature's base walking speed is reduced by 10 feet.

entries.name: No Braaaains
entries: This creature's Intelligence score becomes 3, and cannot be increased by any means.

entries.name: Groaner
entries: This creature cannot speak, but it still understands the languages it knew in life.

entries.name: Decomposing
entries: The magic that binds this creature to undeath does nothing to preserve its body. Over the course of 60 days, the body will rot and crumble to dust, and the creature will die.

entries.name: Fragile Skeleton
entries: The flesh of this creature has long since rotted away, leaving its skeleton exposed. It has vulnerability to bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Endless Undead
entries: Whenever this creature is dealt more than 20 damage from a single attack, part of its corpse is hewn from its body. The body part lands in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it. The body part acts on its own initiative count, uses the {@creature zombie} stat block, and will attack relentlessly until destroyed.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries: The zombie recovers hit points equal to one roll of its hit dice + its Constitution modifier at the start of each of its turns, as long as it was not dealt fire or radiant damage last turn and it still has a head.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the zombie fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: The zombie has 60 feet of blindsight.

entries.name: Carrion Stench
entries: Any creature that starts its turn within 15 feet of the zombie, or moves within 15 feet of it on their turn, must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + Constitution modifier + proficiency bonus) or be {@condition poisoned} until the start of the zombie's next turn. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, they are immune to the zombie's Carrion Stench for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Each creature of the zombie's choice that is within 120 feet of the zombie and aware of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + Charisma modifier + proficiency bonus) or become {@condition frightened} for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the zombie's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Aura of Terror
entries: The zombie has advantage on all attack rolls against {@condition frightened} creatures.

entries.name: Soul Wrench (1/Day)
entries: All {@condition frightened} creatures within 30 feet of the zombie with at least 1 hit point fall to 1 hit point.

entries.name: Unstoppable
entries: Any time the zombie would be reduced to 0 hit points, it drops to 1 hit point instead. This trait does not function if the zombie is decapitated, or was dealt radiant damage this turn.

entries.name: Infection
entries: Any creature killed by this creature is reanimated as a {@creature zombie} under this creature's control at the start of its next turn.

entries.name: How To Train Your Zombie
entries: Sometimes, players or NPCs will seek the means to create their own undead. Although some class features may allow this, here are some general rules that allow anyone to try their hand at necromancy.

items: Any creature type can be Zombified, except undead or constructs.
The traits the creature receives upon being Zombified are at the DM's discretion, chosen from the Zombie Boons and/or Zombie Penalties list.
Any creature reanimated by the Zombification Process obeys its creator's orders without question.

The creator must use their bonus action to command the creature, which can take any action in its stat block, or any other action. If it does not receive a command on a turn, it takes the {@action Dodge} action.
A player can only have one Zombified servant at a time. If they attempt to create another, the present one crumbles to dust.

entries.name: Part 2: Zombification
entries: A player character can attempt to Zombify a creature that has died within the last 24 hours. The process takes a number of hours equal to half the creature's Challenge Rating. During this time, the player character must concentrate as if casting a spell. If at any time their concentration is broken, the Zombification fails and the corpse is destroyed.

Zombification is a magical and technical process that requires specific oils, gemstones, and other exotic materials. The materials required to zombify a creature are equal in value to 500 gp multiplied by the creature's Challenge Rating. These materials are consumed whether or not the Zombification is successful.

At the end of the Zombification process, the player character must make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check (DC = 8 + the creature's Challenge Rating). On a success, the creature is reanimated as an undead under their command. On a failure, the corpse is destroyed.

If the creature actively desired to be revived under the player character's command at the moment it was killed, or the player character killed the creature personally, the DC of the check is reduced by 5.

The Zombification process is complex and shrouded in mystery. It is at the DM's discretion whether a player knows the steps to attempt it. A DM may require a player to undergo a quest to obtain the knowledge.

Zombification is a form of alchemical necromancy magic, and is almost exclusively attempted by evil spellcasters. However, you do not need to be able to cast a spell to attempt the process, and those who harness these secrets in their own vision of good have been known to exist.

variantrule.name: Subclass Multiclassing
entries: Here are a set of variant rules that allow for multiclassing between two subclass options of the same class (referred to as "multi-subclassing").

Multi-subclassing is a complex subject. When using these rules, work closely with your DM and players and adjust them to suit your table. As a word of caution, sticking to the rule that reduces maximum hit points in exchange for multi-subclassing is recommended to balance powerful combinations.

items: You may only multi-subclass once from the same class. For example, you can multi-subclass as a Cleric between the Sky Domain and Life Domain. Once you have multi-subclassed in this way, no more subclasses from the Cleric class can be obtained.

You can only multi-subclass with one of your current classes. For example, a Sorcerer/Warlock multiclass can only multi-subclass in Warlock OR Sorcerer. They cannot hold two subclasses in each discipline.

If multi-subclassing would grant you access to a new spell list, you may choose one spell of each level to build your subclass spell list. Each spell you choose replaces a spell from your original subclass spell list. Multi-subclassing never grants additional prepared spells, only a larger pool of spell options to choose from as your prepared spell list.

You can multi-subclass any time you would receive a subclass feature. In place of that subclass feature, you can instead choose a subclass feature of the same level from a different subclass. You now gain the benefits of that feature in addition to your other class features. For example, a 6th-level Life Domain Cleric can choose, in place of their Blessed Healer feature, to multi-subclass into Sky Domain and gain its 6th-level Sunlight Empowerment feature.

When you multi-subclass, you do not receive additional resources with which to fuel your abilities (e.g., multi-subclassing twice into Warlock will not grant additional Pact Magic slots, and multi-subclassing twice into Cleric will not grant additional uses of Channel Divinity).

If a multi-subclass grants a feature that is dependent on a previous subclass feature which the player doesn't have, they gain any relevant background feature to make the ability usable. For example, taking the 6th-level Draconic Bloodline feature Elemental Affinity requires the selection of a Dragon Ancestor; a character who multi-subclasses into Draconic Sorcerer must select a dragon ancestor to use the feature, but gains no other benefits from that ancestry beyond what is associated with the 6th-level feature.

When you reach the next level you would receive a subclass benefit after multi-subclassing, you may choose to progress in either discipline. Choose one subclass feature of that level from either subclass.

Multi-subclassing between disciplines is extraordinarily taxing on the mind and body. When you multi-subclass, you permanently lose one of your Hit Dice, and your hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to a roll of that die plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1). This reduction cannot be prevented or reduced by any means.

variantrule.name: Drugs in D&D
entries: Introducing illicit substances opens a vast political and social dynamic to your world. Are these substances illegal? What punishment awaits those caught buying and selling them? How will these drugs affect your world and the inhabitants within? Who is producing them, and who is buying them?

All these questions can naturally lead to exciting NPCs, quests, storylines, and character arcs. Here are four sample drugs designed with player use in mind, each offering benefits alongside varying degrees of danger.

entries.name: Pipe Weed
entries: Pipe Weed is a naturally occurring tobacco which grows in warm, wet climates. It is widely distributed and legal in most kingdoms, although its use is strictly prohibited by many faiths, earning it the nickname "Devil Thorn". Primarily consumed for recreational purposes, a particularly potent dose can produce small magical benefits alongside the risk of temporary sickness.
People under the effect of Pipe Weed often display symptoms such as sleepiness, hunger, laziness, and overconfidence.
{@b Cost per potent dose:} 50 gp
Consuming a potent dose of Pipe Weed imparts the following effects, which last for 2 hours:

items: You have disadvantage on all initiative rolls.
You have advantage on saving throws to resist or end the {@condition frightened} condition.
You resist psychic damage.

entries: Consuming too much Pipe Weed can result in sickness. If you consume more than one dose per long rest, you must make a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned} for the next 4 hours.

entries.name: Magical Material Mushrooms
entries: Magical Material Mushrooms are extraordinarily rare fungi that have resisted all efforts at cultivation. Many cultures view their consumption as a test of the gods: if your spirit is pure, you will be granted truths regarding reality; if weak, you will be reduced to a quivering wreck for the next 60 minutes.

Magical Material Mushrooms are highly sought after by wizards as spell components. A Magical Material Mushroom can be used in place of any material component for a spell once, and is dissolved in the casting.
{@b Cost per mushroom:} 1,000 gp
If a creature consumes a Magical Material Mushroom, they must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw:

items: {@b Success:} They cast the {@spell contact other plane} spell, automatically succeeding on the Intelligence saving throw required by the spell. After the spell ends, the creature falls asleep for the next hour, or until roused.
{@b Failure:} The creature becomes {@condition frightened} of a random creature within 60 feet of them at the start of each turn, until the start of their next turn, lasting for 1 hour.

entries: Once a creature has consumed a Magical Material Mushroom, they automatically fail any further saving throws from consuming another within the next {@dice 1d6} years.

entries.name: Glimmer
entries: Glimmer is a curious drug that aims to replicate the magic of elves for other humanoid races. It is extremely costly to produce, appears as a golden liquid, and its production is often outlawed. While a pure batch has no negative side effects, an incorrectly brewed batch can prove deadly with no external way to detect the difference beforehand.
{@b Cost per dose:} 500 gp
While under the effects of Glimmer, you gain the following benefits for the next 12 hours:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks.
You see in nonmagical darkness as if it were dim light, and dim light as if it were bright light, out to a range of 120 feet.
You can take a long rest while doing gentle activities such as reading, keeping watch, or walking at a gentle pace.

entries: Once you use Glimmer, you cannot gain the benefits from the drug again until you complete a long rest while not under its effects.

Additionally, roll a {@dice d10} after ingesting Glimmer. On a 1, the dose is a bad batch: you become {@condition poisoned}, {@condition blinded}, and your Strength, Intelligence, and Charisma scores fall to 3. You cannot take actions, cannot understand speech, and speak only gibberish. A {@spell greater restoration} spell cast on you ends these effects.

entries.name: Tempo
entries: Tempo is an extraordinarily potent, fast-acting, dangerous drug produced in spellcasting laboratories by mixing spell components with unstable magics. It typically comes in the form of a neon blue powder and is favored by mercenaries and bandits for its sudden combat buffs.
{@b Cost per dose:} 200 gp
After taking a dose of Tempo, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

items: Your movement speed is doubled.
Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d4} damage.
You have advantage on initiative rolls.
You have advantage on Dexterity and Intelligence saving throws.
Magic can't put you to sleep.

entries: When the effects of Tempo wear off, you gain one level of {@condition exhaustion}.

In addition, each time you take Tempo, make a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 13 + the number of times you have used Tempo in the last 10 days. On a failed save, you gain none of the benefits of Tempo, immediately take {@damage 6d8} poison damage, and become {@condition paralyzed} for 1 minute. At the end of each of your turns, you can repeat this saving throw, ending the {@condition paralyzed} condition on a success.

variantrule.name: Horde Mode
entries: D&D Horde Mode pits the party against waves of enemies attacking with increasing levels of difficulty, offering a fast-paced combat trial for one-shots or build testing.

items: One or more regular players can't attend, and you want a non-canonical, low-prep session.
Players want to test out new character builds and combinations against varied combat challenges.
The table needs a break from heavy roleplay for pure combat encounters.
New players want to learn combat without the pressure of extensive roleplay.
The group wants to experience high-tier play or extreme difficulty (such as 16th-level play).
You want to hand out wild magic items and boons without breaking a long-term campaign.
Each player begins each wave by being teleported to a random location on the map.
Enemies spawn into the map at random locations, but never more than 3 enemies at once in the same room as a player.

Enemies spawn in waves against the party. Once a wave of enemies enters the battlefield, the next wave cannot enter until all enemies are destroyed or otherwise neutralized at the DM's discretion (e.g., under the effect of {@spell dominate monster}).
Once a wave of enemies is dealt with, the next wave spawns into the map after two full rounds.
If a player character is dead when a new wave begins, all players lose the game (unless using Zombie Horde Rules).

Four invisible magic items appear scattered randomly across the map each wave. A player can locate an item by using an action to make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check while within 30 feet of it. On a success, a chest containing the item materializes. Opening a chest requires a bonus action. When opened, roll a {@dice d20}: on a 20, the player receives the loot and 1 point of inspiration; on a 1, the chest becomes a {@creature mimic}. All unclaimed items vanish during short rests.
Magic items found in Horde Mode are attuned to instantly.
Spell scrolls found in Horde Mode can be used by any player regardless of class or level. If a character lacks a spellcasting feature, they use Constitution as their spellcasting ability.
Players can receive boons upon completing specific challenges set by the DM.
At the DM's discretion, waves of enemies may introduce battlefield effects.
Players receive a short rest after every 3 waves of enemies.
The standard recommended party level for a Zombie Horde Mode is level 8, with 7 waves to complete the run.

entries.name: Variant: Zombie Horde Rules
entries: Under this variant, a player who starts a new wave dead joins the enemy side as a Super Zombie. They cannot use items found on the map or earn challenge rewards. Once destroyed, they reform at the start of each new wave.

Each time the Super Zombie reforms, it gains an additional {@dice 4d10} hit points and a single spell slot. It can cast any Warlock spell of a level equal to or below the number of times it has reformed using Constitution as its spellcasting ability.

entries.name: Suggested Challenges
entries: Challenges allow the DM to reward players for exceptional combat feats with short- or long-rest resources, spell slots, or boons.

entries.name: Non-Combat Rounds and Roleplay
entries: Although Horde Mode focuses primarily on combat, non-combat encounters can break up the action:

items: A {@creature gynosphinx} appears with a riddle for the party to solve in place of a battle.
A complex or lethal puzzle room replaces a combat wave.
A quirky traveling merchant visits during short rests, selling items in exchange for loot and coin gathered during previous waves.
